kumaoni: गौंक जोगी जोगना, आन गौंक सिद्ध।
roman: Gaunk jogi jogana, aan gaunk siddh.
literal_translation: The ascetic of one's own village is merely a beggar, while an ascetic from another village is considered enlightened.
figurative_meaning: Familiarity breeds contempt; people do not value talent or wisdom found in their own home or locality.
hindi_equivalent: घर की मुर्गी दाल बराबर।
english_equivalent: A prophet is never honored in his own country.

kumaoni: भैंसिक आगि बीन बजौण।
roman: Bhainsik aagi been bajaun.
literal_translation: Playing a flute in front of a buffalo.
figurative_meaning: Trying to give good advice or impart wisdom to someone who cannot appreciate or comprehend it.
hindi_equivalent: भैंस के आगे बीन बजाना।
english_equivalent: Casting pearls before swine.

kumaoni: आपण हाथ जगन्नाथ।
roman: Aapan haath Jagannath.
literal_translation: One's own hand is Lord Jagannath.
figurative_meaning: Self-reliance is the greatest virtue; reliance on one's own work brings success.
hindi_equivalent: अपना हाथ जगन्नाथ / आत्मनिर्भरता ही सबसे बड़ा बल है।
english_equivalent: If you want something done right, do it yourself.

kumaoni: कौवा बैठण और डाली भांगण।
roman: Kauwa baithan aur daali bhaangan.
literal_translation: The crow perched and the branch snapped.
figurative_meaning: A pure coincidence that ends up getting blamed on the person who arrived at that moment.
hindi_equivalent: इत्तफ़ाक से हुआ नुकसान किसी के मत्थे मढ़ना।
english_equivalent: A sheer unfortunate coincidence.

kumaoni: बाखरो खाणो न सींग देखणो।
roman: Baakharo khaano na seeng dekhano.
literal_translation: Neither eating the goat nor seeing its horns.
figurative_meaning: Suffering punishment or blame for something without having enjoyed any benefit from it.
hindi_equivalent: बिना किसी लाभ के बदनामी झेलना।
english_equivalent: Blamed for everything without getting anything.

kumaoni: चैतक घाम और जेठक ब्याल।
roman: Chaitak ghaam aur Jethak byaal.
literal_translation: The sunshine of Chait (spring) and the evening breeze of Jeth (summer).
figurative_meaning: Describing things that bring immense comfort and natural delight in the Himalayan hills.
hindi_equivalent: मौसम का सबसे सुखद और मनभावन अहसास।
english_equivalent: The most pleasant blessings of nature.

kumaoni: जाँक घाम, ताँक छाँव।
roman: Jaank ghaam, taank chhaanv.
literal_translation: Where there is sun, there is shadow.
figurative_meaning: Every joyous situation has its trials, and every blessing comes with responsibilities.
hindi_equivalent: जहाँ धूप है, वहीं छाँव भी है।
english_equivalent: Every cloud has a silver lining / Sunshine comes with shadow.

kumaoni: डाली म न चिल्या, घौंसल म न अण्ड।
roman: Daali ma na chilya, ghaunsal ma na and.
literal_translation: Neither bird on tree nor egg in the nest.
figurative_meaning: Being completely empty-handed without any resource or fallback.
hindi_equivalent: पूरी तरह से साधनविहीन होना।
english_equivalent: Having nothing at all to show for one's efforts.

kumaoni: आपणो मरो, स्वर्ग देख्यो।
roman: Aapano maro, swarg dekhyo.
literal_translation: Only when one dies oneself does one see heaven.
figurative_meaning: One learns best and achieves success through firsthand personal struggle and direct experience.
hindi_equivalent: अपने मरे बिना स्वर्ग नहीं दिखता।
english_equivalent: Experience is the best teacher / You must do the work yourself.

kumaoni: जैसि करनी, वैसि भरनी।
roman: Jaisi karani, vaisi bharani.
literal_translation: As you act, so you shall receive.
figurative_meaning: Actions carry natural consequences.
hindi_equivalent: जैसी करनी, वैसी भरनी।
english_equivalent: As you sow, so shall you reap.

kumaoni: द्याप्त देखण जागस्यर, म्यल देखण बागस्यर।
roman: Dyaapt dekhan Jaagasyar, myal dekhan Baagasyar.
literal_translation: To behold the deities go to Jageshwar; to witness the grand folk fair go to Bageshwar.
figurative_meaning: Each place possesses its distinct cultural and spiritual pinnacle; seek things where their true excellence lies.
hindi_equivalent: देव दर्शन के लिए जागेश्वर और मेले के आनंद के लिए बागेश्वर सर्वोत्तम है।
english_equivalent: Go to the source where excellence and tradition truly reside.

kumaoni: अकलक उमरक भेंट न हनू।
roman: Akalak umarak bhent na hanoo.
literal_translation: Wisdom and age do not necessarily meet together.
figurative_meaning: Age alone does not guarantee wisdom, and young people may possess great insight and maturity.
hindi_equivalent: बुद्धि और उम्र का एक साथ होना जरूरी नहीं; समझदारी अनुभव और विचार से आती है।
english_equivalent: Wisdom does not automatically come with age.

kumaoni: अगासकि तारा लुछि ल्होन।
roman: Agaasaki taara luchhi lhon.
literal_translation: Claiming to pluck stars from the sky.
figurative_meaning: Boasting about achieving impossible or impractical feats.
hindi_equivalent: आसमान के तारे तोड़ लाने का दावा करना / असंभव बातें करना।
english_equivalent: Promising the moon / claiming the impossible.

kumaoni: साप कै डरै, लट्ठी से डरस।
roman: Saap kai darai, latthee se daras.
literal_translation: After fearing the snake, one even fears a walking stick.
figurative_meaning: Once a person suffers a severe setback or trauma, even harmless reminders cause apprehension.
hindi_equivalent: दूध का जला छाछ भी फूँक-फूँक कर पीता है।
english_equivalent: Once bitten, twice shy.

kumaoni: घुरि गा भैंस पानी मा।
roman: Ghuri ga bhains paani ma.
literal_translation: The buffalo went back into the mud water again.
figurative_meaning: All hard-earned progress was undone, and matters returned to square one or old flawed habits.
hindi_equivalent: गई भैंस पानी में / सारी मेहनत पर फिर पानी फिर जाना।
english_equivalent: Back to square one / down the drain.

kumaoni: रुखक पात लै हवा बिना नी हल्लान।
roman: Rookhak paat lai hawa bina nee hallan.
literal_translation: Even the leaf of a tree does not shake without the wind.
figurative_meaning: Every event or rumor has an underlying cause or grain of truth.
hindi_equivalent: बिना आग के धुआँ नहीं उठता।
english_equivalent: There is no smoke without fire.

kumaoni: काफल पाको चैत, मेरी छैल नी रैत।
roman: Kaaphal paako Chait, meree chhail nee rait.
literal_translation: The wild Kaaphal berries ripen in spring, yet my beloved does not stay in the shadow.
figurative_meaning: Folk lament expressing the fleeting joy of Himalayan spring and seasonal separation.
hindi_equivalent: काफल पकने की बहार आई, पर प्रियतम का संग न मिला।
english_equivalent: Spring's bounty arrives, yet longing remains unfulfilled.

kumaoni: बूबूक धोती, नातीक जाँघ।
roman: Boobook dhoti, naateek jaangh.
literal_translation: The grandfather's dhoti becomes the grandson's shorts.
figurative_meaning: Illustrates traditional Himalayan thriftiness, sustainable reuse, and generational heritage.
hindi_equivalent: पुरानी चीजों का सदुपयोग और मितव्ययिता।
english_equivalent: Waste not, want not / thrift across generations.

kumaoni: अभागि कौतिक गो, कौतिकै नि है।
roman: Abhaagi koutik go, koutikai ni hai.
literal_translation: The unlucky man went to the fair, and no fair took place.
figurative_meaning: An unlucky person encounters disappointment wherever he goes.
hindi_equivalent: दुर्भाग्यशाली व्यक्ति को कहीं भी सफलता या सुख नहीं मिलता।
english_equivalent: An unlucky person encounters disappointment wherever he goes.
source: Pt. Ganga Datt Upreti (1894) / Kumaoni Folk Wisdom

kumaoni: अघैईं बामणै कि भैंसेन खीर।
roman: Aghaeein baamanai ki bhainsen kheer.
literal_translation: To a full-bellied Brahmin, even buffalo milk kheer has flaws.
figurative_meaning: When one is already satiated or over-indulged, even the best offerings seem inadequate.
hindi_equivalent: तृप्त व्यक्ति को स्वादिष्ट और उत्तम वस्तु में भी नुक्स नजर आते हैं।
english_equivalent: When one is already satiated or over-indulged, even the best offerings seem inadequate.

kumaoni: अकल और उमर कैं कभैं भेट नि हुनि।
roman: Akal aur umar kain kabhain bhet ni huni.
literal_translation: Wisdom and youth never meet.
figurative_meaning: True wisdom only matures with age and experience, rarely in impetuous youth.
hindi_equivalent: बुद्धि और परिपक्वता समय और अनुभव के साथ ही आती है।
english_equivalent: True wisdom only matures with age and experience, rarely in impetuous youth.

kumaoni: अघिन कुकेलि पछिन मिठी।
roman: Aghin kukeli pachhin mithi.
literal_translation: Bitter at first, but sweet in the end.
figurative_meaning: Wholesome advice or hard discipline may taste harsh initially, but yields rewarding results.
hindi_equivalent: सच्ची सीख या अनुशासन शुरुआत में कड़वा लगता है पर परिणाम मधुर होता है।
english_equivalent: Wholesome advice or hard discipline may taste harsh initially, but yields rewarding results.

kumaoni: अपणा जोगि जोगता, पल्ले गौं का संत।
roman: Apna jogi jogta, palle gaun ka sant.
literal_translation: Our own ascetic is just a mendicant, but a distant village's hermit is hailed as a saint.
figurative_meaning: Familiarity breeds contempt; local talents are undervalued while outsiders are praised.
hindi_equivalent: घर के गुणी व्यक्ति की कद्र नहीं होती, बाहर वाले को अधिक सम्मान दिया जाता है (घर का जोगी जोगड़ा, आन गाँव का सिद्ध)।
english_equivalent: Familiarity breeds contempt; local talents are undervalued while outsiders are praised.

kumaoni: अमुसि दिन गौ बल्द लै ठाड़ उठूँ।
roman: Amusi din gau bald lai thaad uthoon.
literal_translation: On the new moon night, even lazy cattle stand up alert.
figurative_meaning: When supreme danger or adversity looms, even the weakest rally all their strength.
hindi_equivalent: विपत्ति आने पर दुर्बल और आलसी व्यक्ति भी आत्मरक्षा के लिए उठ खड़ा होता है।
english_equivalent: When supreme danger or adversity looms, even the weakest rally all their strength.

kumaoni: अन्यारै कि मार खबर नै सार।
roman: Anyaarai ki maar khabar nai saar.
literal_translation: A blow struck in the dark leaves neither evidence nor explanation.
figurative_meaning: Hidden injustices or lack of transparency leave no clue for resolution.
hindi_equivalent: अंधेरे में किया गया कार्य या अपारदर्शी व्यवस्था में सच्चाई का पता नहीं चलता।
english_equivalent: Hidden injustices or lack of transparency leave no clue for resolution.

kumaoni: अस्सी गिचाँ दगड़ि कैलै नि सकि।
roman: Assi gichaan dagdi kailai ni saki.
literal_translation: No one can contend against eighty mouths speaking at once.
figurative_meaning: It is impossible for an individual to stop collective gossip and rumors.
hindi_equivalent: सार्वजनिक अफवाहों और बहुसंख्यक जुबानों को अकेला व्यक्ति नहीं रोक सकता।
english_equivalent: It is impossible for an individual to stop collective gossip and rumors.

kumaoni: अति बिराऊँ में मूस नि मरन।
roman: Ati biraaoon mein moos ni maran.
literal_translation: When there are too many cats, no mouse gets caught.
figurative_meaning: Too many cooks spoil the broth; overcrowded authority creates confusion.
hindi_equivalent: अधिक लोगों के हस्तक्षेप से कार्य बिगड़ जाता है (ज्यादा जोगी मठ उजाड़)।
english_equivalent: Too many cooks spoil the broth; overcrowded authority creates confusion.

kumaoni: ब्याज रात में ले बाट लागि रौं।
roman: Byaaj raat mein le baat laagi raun.
literal_translation: Interest on debt travels along the path even through the night.
figurative_meaning: Debts and interest never cease accumulating, even while you sleep.
hindi_equivalent: कर्ज का ब्याज दिन-रात निरंतर बढ़ता रहता है।
english_equivalent: Debts and interest never cease accumulating, even while you sleep.

kumaoni: बण सुंगरै'ल उज्याड़ खै, गौंक कुकुरै'ल डांड भरी।
roman: Ban sungarail ujyaad khai, gaunk kukurail daand bhari.
literal_translation: The wild boar destroyed the crop, but the village dog paid the penalty.
figurative_meaning: The guilty party escapes into the wild, while an innocent scapegoat is punished.
hindi_equivalent: अपराध कोई करे और सजा किसी निर्दोष को भुगतनी पड़े।
english_equivalent: The guilty party escapes into the wild, while an innocent scapegoat is punished.

kumaoni: नानी खाप, ठुलि धाद।
roman: Naani khaap, thuli dhaad.
literal_translation: A small mouth, but a gigantic shout.
figurative_meaning: Small people making tall, unsubstantiated boasts (small stature, big talk).
hindi_equivalent: छोटा मुँह बड़ी बात करना / सामर्थ्य से अधिक डींगें हांकना।
english_equivalent: Small people making tall, unsubstantiated boasts (small stature, big talk).

kumaoni: जखा बिल्लि नि तखा मूस नाचुनी।
roman: Jakha billi ni takha moos naachuni.
literal_translation: Where the cat is absent, the mice dance.
figurative_meaning: When the supervisor is away, subordinates neglect discipline and make merry.
hindi_equivalent: मुखिया या नियंत्रक की अनुपस्थिति में अनुशासनहीनता फैल जाती है।
english_equivalent: When the supervisor is away, subordinates neglect discipline and make merry.

kumaoni: बाण बणै बल्द हराणो।
roman: Baan banai bald haraano.
literal_translation: Losing the ox while in the middle of ploughing.
figurative_meaning: Extreme absent-mindedness; losing track of the very tool in one's own hands.
hindi_equivalent: अति भूलक्कड़पन, हाथ की चीज को ही तलाशते रहना।
english_equivalent: Extreme absent-mindedness; losing track of the very tool in one's own hands.

kumaoni: अनाल कि चोट कनाल।
roman: Anaal ki chot kanaal.
literal_translation: Aiming at the lower terrace and hitting the upper ridge.
figurative_meaning: Accidental result completely contrary to the original intention.
hindi_equivalent: निशाना कहीं और लगाना और असर कहीं और होना / अनपेक्षित परिणाम।
english_equivalent: Accidental result completely contrary to the original intention.

kumaoni: नाँव नौ ततरो-ततरो, पाणी पीणा को फुट्यूँ पातरो।
roman: Naanw nau tataro-tataro, paani peena ko phutyoon paatro.
literal_translation: Great name and loud reputation, but only a cracked pot to drink water.
figurative_meaning: Hollow grandeur; big reputation on the outside but destitute inside.
hindi_equivalent: नाम बड़े और दर्शन छोटे / दिखावटी शानो-शौकत।
english_equivalent: Hollow grandeur; big reputation on the outside but destitute inside.

kumaoni: कौवा शिकार मारन त बाज को पाल।
roman: Kauwa shikaar maaran ta baaj ko paal.
literal_translation: If crows could hunt prey, who would feed and train a falcon?
figurative_meaning: If unqualified people could do specialized work, experts would not be needed.
hindi_equivalent: यदि अयोग्य व्यक्ति ही कठिन काम कर लेते तो गुणी विशेषज्ञों की आवश्यकता क्यों पड़ती।
english_equivalent: If unqualified people could do specialized work, experts would not be needed.

kumaoni: गाँवक गोरु, गाँवकै ब्यान।
roman: Gaunvak goru, gaunvakai byaan.
literal_translation: The village cattle calve within the village.
figurative_meaning: Village affairs and relationships find their natural resolution within the community.
hindi_equivalent: आपसी मामले और रिश्तेदारी अपने ही समाज और गाँव में भली लगती है।
english_equivalent: Village affairs and relationships find their natural resolution within the community.

kumaoni: घ्याव पडो बामणाक दाढ़ी।
roman: Ghyaav pado baamanaak daadhi.
literal_translation: Clarified butter fell into the Brahmin's beard.
figurative_meaning: An unexpected windfall or fortune benefiting someone perfectly positioned to enjoy it.
hindi_equivalent: अनायास ही किसी प्रिय वस्तु का लाभ मिल जाना।
english_equivalent: An unexpected windfall or fortune benefiting someone perfectly positioned to enjoy it.

kumaoni: धार मलि घाम, तलि मलि ब्याव।
roman: Dhaar mali ghaam, tali mali byaav.
literal_translation: Sun on the mountain crest, wedding festivity echoing across the valley.
figurative_meaning: Good news and sunlight cannot be hidden on the hills.
hindi_equivalent: अच्छी खबर और धूप पहाड़ में कभी छिपी नहीं रहती।
english_equivalent: A city set on a hill cannot be hidden.
source: Dr. Trilochan Pandey (Kumaoni Bhasha Aur Sahitya, 1977)

kumaoni: आफू मरे बिना सरग नी देखिंछ।
roman: Aaphoo mare bina sarag nee dekhinchh.
literal_translation: Without dying oneself, heaven cannot be seen.
figurative_meaning: Self-effort and direct experience are necessary to achieve high outcomes.
hindi_equivalent: बिना खुद मरे स्वर्ग नहीं दिखता (खुद के प्रयास से ही फल मिलता है)।
english_equivalent: If you want something done right, do it yourself.

kumaoni: काकड़ाक मुंड नि, भुंगड़ाक पूंछ नि।
roman: Kaakdaak mund ni, bhungdaak poonch ni.
literal_translation: The cucumber has no distinct head, the roasted grain has no tail.
figurative_meaning: Disorganized speech or action without beginning or end.
hindi_equivalent: बिना सिर-पैर की बात।
english_equivalent: Neither head nor tail.

kumaoni: गौं म घट्ट, बन म लाकड़, पेट म भूख।
roman: Gaun ma ghatt, ban ma laakad, pet ma bhookh.
literal_translation: The watermill in the village, firewood in the forest, and hunger in the stomach.
figurative_meaning: When all resources are nearby, one only needs effort to solve any problem.
hindi_equivalent: साधन पास में हों तो मेहनत से ही काम बनता है।
english_equivalent: Where there is a will, there is a way.

kumaoni: डाली म काफल, मन म लालच।
roman: Daali ma kaaphal, man ma laalach.
literal_translation: Wild berries on high branches, longing in the human heart.
figurative_meaning: Temptation of sweet things that require arduous climbing to reach.
hindi_equivalent: ऊंचे फल देखकर मन ललचाना।
english_equivalent: The sweetest fruit hangs highest on the tree.

kumaoni: घाम तापा, पाणि पिवा, निरोगी रया।
roman: Ghaam taapa, paani piwa, nirogi raya.
literal_translation: Bask in the mountain sun, drink pure spring water, and stay healthy.
figurative_meaning: Simplicity and natural living in the Himalayas ensure a disease-free life.
hindi_equivalent: प्राकृतिक जीवन शैली से ही उत्तम स्वास्थ्य संभव है।
english_equivalent: Nature is the best physician.

kumaoni: आपण हाथ जगन्नाथ, आपण गोठ अन्नदाता।
roman: Aapan haath Jagannaath, aapan goth annadaata.
literal_translation: One's own hands are Lord Jagannath, one's own cattle barn provides food.
figurative_meaning: Self-reliance, hard labor and agriculture are the true foundation of wealth and dignity.
hindi_equivalent: स्वावलंबन और अपनी मेहनत ही सबसे बड़ा सहारा है।
english_equivalent: God helps those who help themselves.

kumaoni: हिमालयक पाथर मजबूत, कुमाऊँनी की बात पक्की।
roman: Himaalayak paathar majboot, Kumaoni ki baat pakki.
literal_translation: As solid as the slate of the Himalayas, so is the pledged word of a Kumaoni.
figurative_meaning: Integrity, honor, and unshakeable commitment to one's word.
hindi_equivalent: वचनबद्धता और सत्यनिष्ठा ही सबसे बड़ा धर्म है।
english_equivalent: A person's word is their bond.

kumaoni: आपू मरे बिना सुरग नी देखिण।
roman: Aapu mare bina surag ni dekhin.
hindi: स्वयं मरे बिना स्वर्ग नहीं दिखता (काम स्वयं करने पर ही फल मिलता है)।
english: One cannot see heaven without dying oneself (You must do the hard work yourself to achieve success).
figurative_meaning: स्वयं मरे बिना स्वर्ग नहीं दिखता (काम स्वयं करने पर ही फल मिलता है)।
literal_translation: One cannot see heaven without dying oneself (You must do the hard work yourself to achieve success).
hindi_equivalent: स्वयं मरे बिना स्वर्ग नहीं दिखता (काम स्वयं करने पर ही फल मिलता है)।
english_equivalent: One cannot see heaven without dying oneself (You must do the hard work yourself to achieve success).
source: Traditional Kumaoni Akhaan (Pt. Ganga Datt Upreti / Dr. Trilochan Pande)

kumaoni: जाँ घाम ताँ छाम।
roman: Jaan ghaam taan chhaam.
hindi: जहाँ धूप है, वहीं छाया भी है (सुख और दुःख साथ-साथ चलते हैं)।
english: Where there is sunshine, there is also shade (Joy and sorrow go hand in hand).
figurative_meaning: जहाँ धूप है, वहीं छाया भी है (सुख और दुःख साथ-साथ चलते हैं)।
literal_translation: Where there is sunshine, there is also shade (Joy and sorrow go hand in hand).
hindi_equivalent: जहाँ धूप है, वहीं छाया भी है (सुख और दुःख साथ-साथ चलते हैं)।
english_equivalent: Where there is sunshine, there is also shade (Joy and sorrow go hand in hand).
source: Traditional Kumaoni Akhaan (Pt. Ganga Datt Upreti / Dr. Trilochan Pande)

kumaoni: डाना का बासा, घाम का भरोसा।
roman: Daana ka baasa, ghaam ka bharosa.
hindi: पहाड़ की चोटी पर बसेरा धूप के भरोसे होता है (कठिन परिस्थिति में प्राकृतिक साधनों पर निर्भरता)।
english: Living on a mountain peak relies on sunlight (In tough terrains, one depends on nature's mercy).
figurative_meaning: पहाड़ की चोटी पर बसेरा धूप के भरोसे होता है (कठिन परिस्थिति में प्राकृतिक साधनों पर निर्भरता)।
literal_translation: Living on a mountain peak relies on sunlight (In tough terrains, one depends on nature's mercy).
hindi_equivalent: पहाड़ की चोटी पर बसेरा धूप के भरोसे होता है (कठिन परिस्थिति में प्राकृतिक साधनों पर निर्भरता)।
english_equivalent: Living on a mountain peak relies on sunlight (In tough terrains, one depends on nature's mercy).
source: Traditional Kumaoni Akhaan (Pt. Ganga Datt Upreti / Dr. Trilochan Pande)

kumaoni: अंग्वाव का घाव, पछाड़ को ताव।
roman: Angwaav ka ghaav, pachhaad ko taav.
hindi: आगे का घाव वीरता है, पीछे का घाव कायरता।
english: Wounds in front signify courage, wounds on the back reveal cowardice.
figurative_meaning: आगे का घाव वीरता है, पीछे का घाव कायरता।
literal_translation: Wounds in front signify courage, wounds on the back reveal cowardice.
hindi_equivalent: आगे का घाव वीरता है, पीछे का घाव कायरता।
english_equivalent: Wounds in front signify courage, wounds on the back reveal cowardice.
source: Traditional Kumaoni Akhaan (Pt. Ganga Datt Upreti / Dr. Trilochan Pande)

kumaoni: काकड़ का सींग नी हुना।
roman: Kakad ka seeng ni huna.
hindi: काकड़ हिरण के सींग नहीं होते (असंभव बात की आशा करना व्यर्थ है)।
english: A barking deer has no horns (Do not expect impossible things).
figurative_meaning: काकड़ हिरण के सींग नहीं होते (असंभव बात की आशा करना व्यर्थ है)।
literal_translation: A barking deer has no horns (Do not expect impossible things).
hindi_equivalent: काकड़ हिरण के सींग नहीं होते (असंभव बात की आशा करना व्यर्थ है)।
english_equivalent: A barking deer has no horns (Do not expect impossible things).
source: Traditional Kumaoni Akhaan (Pt. Ganga Datt Upreti / Dr. Trilochan Pande)

kumaoni: काफल पाक्यो मैल नी चाख्यो।
roman: Kafal pakyo mail ni chaakhyo.
hindi: काफल पक गए पर मैंने चखे नहीं (सुअवसर हाथ से निकल जाने का विलाप - कफू पक्षी की लोककथा)।
english: The bayberries ripened but I did not taste them (A lament of missed opportunity from the Kafu bird folklore).
figurative_meaning: काफल पक गए पर मैंने चखे नहीं (सुअवसर हाथ से निकल जाने का विलाप - कफू पक्षी की लोककथा)।
literal_translation: The bayberries ripened but I did not taste them (A lament of missed opportunity from the Kafu bird folklore).
hindi_equivalent: काफल पक गए पर मैंने चखे नहीं (सुअवसर हाथ से निकल जाने का विलाप - कफू पक्षी की लोककथा)।
english_equivalent: The bayberries ripened but I did not taste them (A lament of missed opportunity from the Kafu bird folklore).
source: Traditional Kumaoni Akhaan (Pt. Ganga Datt Upreti / Dr. Trilochan Pande)

kumaoni: दुधैं को जळ्यो छांछ फूँकिबेर पीन्छ।
roman: Dudhai ko jalyo chhaanchh foonkiber peench.
hindi: दूध का जला छाछ भी फूँक-फूँक कर पीता है।
english: Once bitten by hot milk, one blows even on cold buttermilk before drinking.
figurative_meaning: दूध का जला छाछ भी फूँक-फूँक कर पीता है।
literal_translation: Once bitten by hot milk, one blows even on cold buttermilk before drinking.
hindi_equivalent: दूध का जला छाछ भी फूँक-फूँक कर पीता है।
english_equivalent: Once bitten by hot milk, one blows even on cold buttermilk before drinking.
source: Traditional Kumaoni Akhaan (Pt. Ganga Datt Upreti / Dr. Trilochan Pande)

kumaoni: जिले खाणो भात, उल नी देखणी रात।
roman: Jile khaano bhaat, ul ni dekhni raat.
hindi: जिसने मेहनत से भात खाना है, वह रात-दिन की परवाह नहीं करता।
english: He who desires a good meal does not count the dark hours of toil.
figurative_meaning: जिसने मेहनत से भात खाना है, वह रात-दिन की परवाह नहीं करता।
literal_translation: He who desires a good meal does not count the dark hours of toil.
hindi_equivalent: जिसने मेहनत से भात खाना है, वह रात-दिन की परवाह नहीं करता।
english_equivalent: He who desires a good meal does not count the dark hours of toil.
source: Traditional Kumaoni Akhaan (Pt. Ganga Datt Upreti / Dr. Trilochan Pande)

kumaoni: घरैं को जोगी जोगड़ा, आन गाँव को सिद्ध।
roman: Gharai ko jogi jogada, aan gaanv ko siddh.
hindi: घर का जोगी जोगड़ा, आन गाँव का सिद्ध (घर की प्रतिभा का आदर नहीं होता)।
english: A local hermit is dismissed, while a stranger from another village is revered as a sage.
figurative_meaning: घर का जोगी जोगड़ा, आन गाँव का सिद्ध (घर की प्रतिभा का आदर नहीं होता)।
literal_translation: A local hermit is dismissed, while a stranger from another village is revered as a sage.
hindi_equivalent: घर का जोगी जोगड़ा, आन गाँव का सिद्ध (घर की प्रतिभा का आदर नहीं होता)।
english_equivalent: A local hermit is dismissed, while a stranger from another village is revered as a sage.
source: Traditional Kumaoni Akhaan (Pt. Ganga Datt Upreti / Dr. Trilochan Pande)

kumaoni: नाच नी जाणो आँगण तेड़ो।
roman: Naach ni jaano aangan tedo.
hindi: नाचना नहीं आता तो आँगन को टेढ़ा बताना (अपनी अक्षमता का दोष दूसरों पर मढ़ना)।
english: A poor dancer blames the crooked courtyard.
figurative_meaning: नाचना नहीं आता तो आँगन को टेढ़ा बताना (अपनी अक्षमता का दोष दूसरों पर मढ़ना)।
literal_translation: A poor dancer blames the crooked courtyard.
hindi_equivalent: नाचना नहीं आता तो आँगन को टेढ़ा बताना (अपनी अक्षमता का दोष दूसरों पर मढ़ना)।
english_equivalent: A poor dancer blames the crooked courtyard.
source: Traditional Kumaoni Akhaan (Pt. Ganga Datt Upreti / Dr. Trilochan Pande)

kumaoni: गंगोली को लाटो, पंच बाण्ट खादी एक बाण्ट आटो।
roman: Gangoli ko laato, panch baant khaadi ek baant aato.
literal_translation: The apparent simpleton of Gangoli gives five measures of coarse chaff and takes away one measure of pure flour.
figurative_meaning: Hill folk who seem rustic and guileless often possess deep practical sharpness and will not be easily cheated.
hindi_equivalent: सीधा दीखे पर अक्ल में पूरा।
english_equivalent: Still waters run deep; appearance of simplicity conceals acute wit.

kumaoni: एक गोली का दुइ गोली द्यूँ, अलाई-बलाई शिरा पर ल्यूँ।
roman: Ek goli ka dui goli dyoon, alai-balai shira par lyoon.
literal_translation: Why should one pay two silver coins for one borrowed, and invite calamities and vassalage upon one's head?
figurative_meaning: Indebtedness brings bondage; borrowing at usurious rates ruins freedom and self-respect.
hindi_equivalent: कर्ज से बुरा कोई बंधन नहीं।
english_equivalent: The borrower is servant to the lender.

kumaoni: सौ की सौ, बियाँ की नता।
roman: Sau ki sau, biyaan ki nata.
literal_translation: All hundred spent, not even a single grain left for tomorrow's seed.
figurative_meaning: Reckless expenditure leaves nothing for the future, jeopardizing the next season's harvest.
hindi_equivalent: सब कुछ लुटा कर दाने-दाने को तरसना।
english_equivalent: Penny wise and pound foolish; eating the seed corn.

kumaoni: तीन बोलाया तेरह आया, देखो यांकी रीत। भैरा वाला खाई गया, घरा का गाणी गीत।
roman: Teen bolaaya tera aaya, dekho yaanki reet. Bhaira waala khaai gaya, ghara ka gaani geet.
literal_translation: Three were invited but thirteen showed up; strangers consumed the feast while the household was left singing songs on empty stomachs.
figurative_meaning: Unmanaged hospitality where uninvited freeloaders take the reward while the hardworking host starves.
hindi_equivalent: पराया माल चाट गए, घर वाले ताकते रह गए।
english_equivalent: Uninvited guests eat the host out of hearth and home.

kumaoni: सराद लागा बामण जागा, सराद निमड़ा बामण चिमड़ा।
roman: Saraad laaga baaman jaaga, saraad nimda baaman chimda.
literal_translation: When the ancestor memorial season (Shraddha) begins, the priest awakens with energy; when it concludes, he grows thin and weary.
figurative_meaning: Opportunists show tremendous enthusiasm only while personal profit and free feasts are flowing.
hindi_equivalent: मतलब के यार, काम खत्म तो व्यवहार खत्म।
english_equivalent: Fair-weather friends feast while the sun shines.

kumaoni: ब्योल मरौ ब्योलि, दक्षिणा लिण म्यर काम।
roman: Byol marau byoli, dakshina lin myar kaam.
literal_translation: Whether the groom perishes or the bride survives, collecting the ceremonial fee is my sole concern.
figurative_meaning: Cold, professional self-interest showing utter apathy to the client's actual welfare.
hindi_equivalent: अपना काम बनता, भाड़ में जाए जनता।
english_equivalent: A mercenary cares only for his wage, not the cause.

kumaoni: पोथी न पातड़ी, नाम नरेण पंडित।
roman: Pothi na paatadi, naam Naren Pandit.
literal_translation: Neither possessing holy scripture nor an astrological almanac, yet flaunting the grand title of Master Narayan Pandit.
figurative_meaning: Pretending to hold great erudition and wisdom without an ounce of genuine qualification.
hindi_equivalent: गांठ में नहीं कौड़ी, नाम नवाब साहब।
english_equivalent: An empty vessel makes the greatest sound.

kumaoni: खसियै की रीस, भैंस की तीस।
roman: Khasiyai ki rees, bhains ki tees.
literal_translation: The quick anger of a hill cultivator is as sudden as the huge thirst of a wallowing buffalo.
figurative_meaning: Passionate hill anger flares swiftly over land and honor but subsides just as quickly once justice is served.
hindi_equivalent: क्षणिक क्रोध पर गहरी भावना।
english_equivalent: A spark flares hot and swiftly cools.

kumaoni: गड़ा जामौ झौ, गौं पैठो सौ।
roman: Gada jaamau jhau, gaun paitho sau.
literal_translation: Noxious Jhau weed overtaking a terraced field is as ruinous as an unscrupulous moneylender establishing himself in a hill hamlet.
figurative_meaning: Exploitative debt destroys rural autonomy just as invasive wild weeds strangle mountain grain.
hindi_equivalent: खेत में खरपतवार और गांव में साहूकार, दोनों का परिणाम बर्बादी।
english_equivalent: An usurer in a village is a blight upon the harvest.

kumaoni: जिमदार हुणि विचार ने, भैंस हुणि कच्यार ने।
roman: Jimdaar huni vichaar ne, bhains huni kachyaar ne.
literal_translation: The stubborn farmer cares nothing for elaborate theories, just as the wallowing water buffalo minds no mud.
figurative_meaning: Practical mountain cultivators care only for tangible harvest and direct reality, ignoring abstract pretenses.
hindi_equivalent: सीधे-साधे स्वभाव में दिखावे का कोई स्थान नहीं।
english_equivalent: Hard work heeds no idle talk.

kumaoni: स्यापक जी ख्वार में, बणियक ढेपु में।
roman: Syaapak jee khwaar me, baniyak dhepu me.
literal_translation: The venomous serpent's life rests in its skull; the miserly trader's life rests in his copper coins.
figurative_meaning: A hoarder holds his treasure dearer than honor, kinship, or virtue.
hindi_equivalent: चमड़ी जाए पर दमड़ी न जाए।
english_equivalent: The miser loves his gold more than his life.

kumaoni: रणमुखी छत्री, तीरथमुखी बामण।
roman: Ranmukhi chhatree, teerathmukhi baaman.
literal_translation: The warrior looks forward toward the field of battle; the devout scholar looks toward the sacred Himalayan shrines.
figurative_meaning: Every individual finds honor in fulfilling their genuine duty and spiritual calling with excellence.
hindi_equivalent: स्वधर्म में ही मनुष्य की शोभा है।
english_equivalent: Every craftsperson honors their own calling.

kumaoni: हँसि हँसि ब्वारिल नौ रोटि खाती।
roman: Hansi hansi bwaaril nau roti khaati.
literal_translation: Laughing cheerily all the while, the daughter-in-law devoured nine loaves of hearth bread.
figurative_meaning: Doing significant damage or consuming major resources behind an innocent, pleasant smile.
hindi_equivalent: मीठी छुरी बन कर काम निकालना।
english_equivalent: A smiling face may conceal a voracious appetite.

kumaoni: बगर्क देखि साग, स्यैणिक देखि बाघ।
roman: Bagark dekhi saag, syainik dekhi baagh.
literal_translation: Wild greens spotted by a man, and a prowling leopard spotted by a woman — both require healthy skepticism.
figurative_meaning: Mountain rumors often exaggerate: men overestimate bountiful forage while anxious women fear hidden hill predators.
hindi_equivalent: सुनी-सुनाई बात की तहकीकात जरूरी है।
english_equivalent: Believe half of what you see and none of what you hear in fear.

kumaoni: धाण कर ब्वारी सगत न्हा, खाण हूँ आ ब्वारी ठूळ थालि कां?
roman: Dhaan kar bwaari sagat nha, khaan hoon aa bwaari thool thaali kaan?
literal_translation: When asked to husk paddy the daughter-in-law groans with exhaustion; when called for the feast she brings the biggest copper plate.
figurative_meaning: Shrinking from labor while running first in line to enjoy the fruits of communal work.
hindi_equivalent: काम से जी चुराना, खाने में आगे आना।
english_equivalent: Idle at work, foremost at the table.

kumaoni: गौं बिगाड़ो राँड़, भात बिगाड़ो माँड़।
roman: Gaun bigaado raand, bhaat bigaado maand.
literal_translation: A venomous slanderer ruins the harmony of a village, just as excess unwashed starch ruins cooked rice.
figurative_meaning: Discord-sowing gossip destroys peaceful hamlets just as poor cooking spoils good food.
hindi_equivalent: कलह से घर और समाज का विनाश होता है।
english_equivalent: A single slanderer can poison a whole community.

kumaoni: सौण भरी सासु, भदौ आए आँसु।
roman: Saun bhari saasu, bhadau aaye aansu.
literal_translation: The mother-in-law passed away in the lush monsoon month of Saun, but the weeping tears arrived only in Bhado.
figurative_meaning: Delayed, affected, or insincere mourning performed only when observers are watching.
hindi_equivalent: दिखावटी शोक / बनावटी रोना।
english_equivalent: Crocodile tears shed long after the deed.

kumaoni: मुट्ठी को धन, मुख कि ज्वे।
roman: Mutthi ko dhan, mukh ki jwe.
literal_translation: Only the wealth physically held in one's clenched fist and the spouse standing in front of one are truly one's own.
figurative_meaning: Theoretical claims and absent relatives offer no security; only what is immediate and tangible can be relied upon.
hindi_equivalent: हाथ का पैसा और सामने का साथी ही अपना है।
english_equivalent: A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.

kumaoni: दाइ हुणि के पेट लुकौण।
roman: Daai huni ke pet lukaun.
literal_translation: What purpose does it serve to hide one's swollen belly from the village midwife?
figurative_meaning: It is futile to conceal the truth from the doctor, teacher, or confidant tasked with helping you.
hindi_equivalent: वैद्य और दाई से क्या भेद छुपाना।
english_equivalent: Hide nothing from your physician and your advocate.

kumaoni: जै बुड़ियाक दुखेल न्यार भे, ऊ म्यर बान आए।
roman: Jai budiyaak dukhel nyaar bhe, oo myar baan aaye.
literal_translation: The cantankerous old grandmother because of whose quarrels the brothers divided the estate ended up assigned to my hearth.
figurative_meaning: Trying hard to escape a nuisance only to find that the entire burden has fallen directly back on your shoulders.
hindi_equivalent: जिस मुसीबत से भागे, वही गले आ पड़ी।
english_equivalent: Out of the frying pan into the fire.

kumaoni: मुसकि ऐ रै गाउ, बिराउक है री खेल।
roman: Musaki ai rai gaau, biraauk hai ree khel.
literal_translation: A dire crisis has befallen the mouse, while for the cat it is mere sport.
figurative_meaning: What is life and death tragedy for the helpless is casual amusement for the powerful.
hindi_equivalent: चूहे की जान पर बनी है और बिल्ली के लिए खेल हो रहा है।
english_equivalent: One man's sorrow is another man's sport.

kumaoni: जो गौं जाण नै, वीक बाट के पुछण।
roman: Jo gaun jaan nai, veek baat ke puchhan.
literal_translation: Why inquire about the road leading to a village you do not intend to visit?
figurative_meaning: Do not waste time or curiosity meddling with affairs that do not concern you.
hindi_equivalent: जिस गाँव जाना नहीं, उसका रास्ता पूछने से क्या लाभ।
english_equivalent: Do not cross bridges you never intend to walk / Mind your own business.

kumaoni: भैंसक सींग भैंस कैं भारर कन हुन।
roman: Bhainsak seeng bhains kain bhaarar kan hoon.
literal_translation: A buffalo's heavy horns are never a burden to the buffalo itself.
figurative_meaning: Parents never consider their own children or family duties an oppressive burden.
hindi_equivalent: भैंस के सींग भैंस को भारी नहीं लगते (अपनी संतान कभी बोझ नहीं होती)।
english_equivalent: A mother never finds the weight of her children burdensome.

kumaoni: आपण सुन ख्वट, परखनेर कै दोष दी।
roman: Aapan sun khwat, parakhner kai dosh dee.
literal_translation: When one's own gold is debased alloy, why cast blame upon the assayer?
figurative_meaning: When one's own people or actions are fundamentally deficient, do not blame the impartial judge.
hindi_equivalent: अपना सोना खोटा हो तो परखने वाले जौहरी को क्या दोष देना।
english_equivalent: Look to your own shortcomings before blaming the evaluator.

kumaoni: द्याप्त देखण जागस्यर, म्याल देखण बागस्यर।
roman: Dyaapt dekhan Jaagasyar, myaal dekhan Baagasyar.
literal_translation: To see deities visit Jageshwar; to behold the grand festival visit Bageshwar.
figurative_meaning: Every sacred Himalayan center possesses its own distinctive cultural virtue and renown.
hindi_equivalent: देवता दर्शन जागेश्वर धाम में और विशाल मेला दर्शन बागेश्वर में।
english_equivalent: To each sanctuary its distinct virtue; to each sacred place its true renown.

kumaoni: जॉ कुकड़ि कन हुन, वॉ के रात कन ब्यानी?
roman: Jau kukadi kan hoon, vau ke raat kan byaani?
literal_translation: In a place where no rooster crows, does the dawn fail to break?
figurative_meaning: Nature's course and society's wheels turn inexorably; no single person is indispensable.
hindi_equivalent: जहाँ मुर्गा नहीं बोलता, क्या वहाँ सवेरा नहीं होता?
english_equivalent: The dawn does not wait for any single rooster to crow.

kumaoni: नानतिनाक जाड़ ढुंगा में।
roman: Naanatinaak jaad dhunga mein.
literal_translation: The winter cold of little children is absorbed harmlessly into mountain rocks.
figurative_meaning: Young children are naturally resilient, active, and impervious to the mountain chill.
hindi_equivalent: बच्चों की सर्दी पत्थर में समा जाती है (बच्चे जाड़े से नहीं डरते)।
english_equivalent: Children are made of sturdy mountain grit.

kumaoni: अदपुरि विद्या जीवे काल।
roman: Adapoori vidya jeeve kaal.
literal_translation: Half-acquired knowledge becomes the very death of life.
figurative_meaning: Superficial understanding causes far more disaster and harm than honest ignorance.
hindi_equivalent: अधूरी विद्या जान की दुश्मन बन जाती है (नीम हकीम खतरा-ए-जान)।
english_equivalent: A little learning is a dangerous thing.

kumaoni: जैक बकड़-बकड़ आस, उइले दे कौन् को गास।
roman: Jaik bakad-bakad aas, uile de kaun ko gaas.
literal_translation: From whom huge hopes were cherished, he offered merely a tiny bite of coarse millet.
figurative_meaning: Grand expectations from self-important patrons frequently result in meager disappointment.
hindi_equivalent: जिससे बड़ी-बड़ी आशाएँ थीं, उसने बहुत मामूली सहारा दिया।
english_equivalent: Great promises often yield very small fruits.

kumaoni: ढको द्वार, हिटो हरिद्वार।
roman: Dhako dwaar, hito Haridwaar.
literal_translation: Shut the home's doors and set off on the pilgrimage to Haridwar.
figurative_meaning: When all worldly ties and domestic disputes become overwhelming, renounce and seek solace.
hindi_equivalent: घर का दरवाजा बंद करो और हरिद्वार की राह पकड़ो (सब छोड़ कर निकल पड़ना)।
english_equivalent: Cut your losses and seek spiritual peace.
